Welcome to the release notes for Update 1.22 Operation: Echoes! This update includes visual overhauls for two classic maps, the long-awaited return of two iconic SMGs, and a fresh round of gear sets, weapon skins, and character customization options.

In Operation: Echoes, we’re turning our attention to two of our older maps: Power Plant and Hideout. We’ve given these a visual pass; you can expect better visuals across the board, from more detailed interiors and exteriors to refined map geometry.
[dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/HB6NfpOOQ9Y"][dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/9W4LkFsY9eY"]

Two familiar heavy-hitters are stepping back onto the frontlines. With Operation: Echoes, we’re welcoming back the UM45 and the MP40 to your loadouts. Combining modern stopping power with timeless precision, these SMGs offer the mobility and reliable performance you need when clearing room to room.

Welcome to the release notes for Update 1.21 Operation: Breachpoint! This update includes a brand-new map, two stylish new pistols, and additional customization options for both factions.

We are excited to introduce our new map, Hold! We showed a brief teaser in the patch notes for the last update, and now it's officially here. Set in a police station under siege, Hold immerses players in intense, close-quarters engagements with restricted sightlines. Navigate a high-security complex where every room could be an ambush. Engage in intense battles throughout cell blocks, conference rooms, and narrow hallways!

items.text: Hello soldiers!

Welcome to the release notes for Update 1.20 Operation: Clear Sight! This update features two new sights, new difficult challenges to grind, mod editor improvements, and new cosmetics for both factions!

First things first, take a look at our upcoming new map, Hold, coming next update (Update 1.21 Operation: ███████). Inspired by Ministry, it features a police station caught in a violent takeover by Insurgent forces. WIP images below!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32965397/e0d11266fa9d01791f001a8bd0e0208b28aa83f5.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32965397/b0175ead3080ce190cbe639094dfaf5ca50a684b.png"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32965397/18ed8ea233281a3bd45a88d1556c7ff56a5e3bfb.png"]Insurgency's origins are deeply rooted in modding. Starting as a mod for the Source engine, Insurgency: Modern Infantry Combat led to a standalone sequel released in 2014 that we’re sure many of you are familiar with, called Insurgency, and then on to Insurgency: Sandstorm.

It's important to remember our roots, and mod support is one way of fulfilling that for the team. We know the modding community has felt left behind in recent years, especially as the release on consoles led our focus to expand. We know the modding tools have been deteriorating.

This leads us to today. We have been working with many from the modding community over the last two updates to address issues flagged for us as important and to add features that should help make even cooler stuff. This one's been coming for a long time, including addressing requests like access to our Wwise project, which is included in this update. This grants modders more creative freedom when incorporating custom sounds into their projects. A guide is available to help mod creators here.

Additionally, we've taken significant steps to improve the content-creation experience in the editor. Modders can now upload mods larger than 2GB directly through the editor. This should help streamline the publishing process. Because the workflow has changed, we've created a guide that walks through the process of creating, uploading, and updating mods.

Finally, we’d like to acknowledge members of the modding community who have stood by us throughout the years. They have spent countless hours creating awesome content that many of you know, including maps from our mapping contest, like Prison and Last Light.

In our previous update, Operation: Shell Shock, we introduced Challenges as a way for players to earn rewards while playing Insurgency: Sandstorm. We’re building on top of that foundation by introducing Tier 3 Challenges. These will raise the bar with more demanding objectives built for those ready to prove their experience and skill.
Here are a few challenges that you can expect to have to grind for:
Kill 500 enemies with Fire Support as a Commander.
Win 100 rounds without dying (good luck!).
Perform 500 headshots with a sidearm.

Hello again soldiers!

Welcome to the release notes for Update 1.17 Operation: Resurgence! The leaves are bare, the smell of snow is in the air, and if you’re anything like us you’ve already eaten enough snacks to incapacitate a small herd of reindeer. What better way to celebrate this holiday season than another major update from the military FPS that just won’t quit! (You may have said, “presents that I asked for” or even “spending time with my loved ones” but we’ve crunched the numbers and it turns out this update is the best way.)

Buckle up folks, it’s happening, CROSSPLAY IS HERE! It’s been a long time coming and we are incredibly happy to be rolling this feature out to you! So, without further ado let’s get to the explaining part because we’re sure you have a lot of questions!

Well you see, when two people love each other very much, sometimes they......what’s that? Oh not the…..uh-huh…..ok right. Got it. AS WE WERE SAYING, crossplay is a new feature that will allow PSN, Xbox Live, and PC players to play together!
How does it work?

Starting with Update 1.17 Operation: Resurgence you will see a “Matchmaking settings” option in place of the “Region settings” option. By selecting it, you will have the following options to choose from:
Your preferred input device from your connected devices (Mouse & Keyboard or Gamepad).
An option to either enable or disable Cross-Play.
An option to match with players using different input devices.
Your selected regions.
Once you’ve filled in your matchmaking settings, you will be matched according to your chosen options!
👀 For more information see our handy-dandy crossplay FAQ!
You heard that right, it’s the return of Skirmish! We’ve gone back to the drawing board and made some changes to freshen the mode up to reintroduce it as a limited-time game mode.

Skirmish pits two 14-player teams (10v10 on console) against each other as they fight to be the first to capture three objectives and blow up the enemy cache. Each team starts with one owned objective, one cache and 10 spawn waves, with the remaining neutral objective in the middle.
Teams can gain additional spawn waves by capturing an objective, but beware! If your team's cache is destroyed you will be unable to gain new waves.

items.text: Hello Sandstorm community!

Welcome to Operation: Accolade, the update where we are privileged to bring you content inspired by the fantastic submissions we received to our mapping and cosmetic community contests!
